root_cause_label: Incomplete NumPy Compatibility Fixes with Wrong Interpreter Environment
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built Cython extensions against the wrong Python interpreter (3.11 with NumPy 2.3.5 instead of 3.12/NumPy 2.3.0) and only partially fixed deprecated NumPy aliases, leaving n.int usages unfixed in openknot.py, knot.py, and dtnotation.py while claiming success after running only a subset of tests.
t_err_evidence: Step 23: Agent installs NumPy 2.3.5 into system Python 3.11 via /usr/bin/python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages cython numpy, overriding the required NumPy 2.3.0 and targeting the wrong interpreter (3.11 instead of the active 3.12 venv), establishing the wrong execution environment for all subsequent work.
t_commit_evidence: Step 65: After discovering remaining n.int usages in openknot.py, knot.py, and dtnotation.py at step 60 but only fixing representation.py (steps 62-63), the agent runs only test_knot.py and test_spacecurve.py (18 passed), treats this as full success, then proceeds to install the package and claim completion without fixing the remaining deprecated aliases or running the full evaluation test suite.
t_surface_evidence: Step 59: pytest run reveals AttributeError: module 'numpy' has no attribute 'int' in representation.py during test_reconstructed_space_curve, surfacing the pattern of remaining deprecated NumPy aliases that affect multiple files beyond what the agent ultimately fixes.
trigger_explanation: At step 23 the agent committed to the wrong Python interpreter environment (system Python 3.11 with NumPy 2.3.5) without first verifying whether this matched the evaluation requirements (Python 3.12 venv with NumPy 2.3.0). Later, at step 65, the agent declared completion after running only two test files (test_knot.py, test_spacecurve.py) without ensuring all deprecated numpy aliases were fixed across the full codebase discovered at step 60 (openknot.py, knot.py, dtnotation.py still had n.int usages).
forewarning_evidence: Step 7: build fell back to Python-only mode ('Cython or numpy could not be imported') despite both being installed, signaling environment mismatch. Steps 11-12: ModuleNotFoundError for Cython under the active Python interpreter despite pip showing it installed for Python 3.13/3.11, confirming multi-interpreter confusion. Step 60: grep reveals n.int in 5 files (openknot.py lines 305/480/683/1152/1162, knot.py line 315, dtnotation.py lines 55/73) but agent only fixes 2 lines in representation.py.
